chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whatever of the birds arrays (its wings in flight), so it is not for you to take it out (from the Haram), and whatever does not array (its wings in flight), so it is for you to take it out.
He said, 'And I asked him about the Ethiopian chicken (Turkey).' He said, 'It is not from the game (hunted birds). Rather, the game is what flies between the sky and the earth.'

key_terms.بَيْنَ السَّمَاءِ وَ الْأَرْضِ: Between the sky and the earth
key_terms.تُخْرِجَهُ: To take it out (from the Haram)
key_terms.يَصُفُّ: To array or line up (wings in flight)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on slaughtering birds like Turkey inside the Haram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the boundaries of permissible game within the Haram by distinguishing between birds that fly in organized formations (true game) and those that do not, specifically exempting the Ethiopian chicken (turkey) due to its lower flight pattern. Scholarly interpretation highlights this as a practical application of the general principle that 'game' implies wild creatures roaming between sky and earth, thereby allowing pilgrims to consume domesticated or low-flying birds without violating the sanctity of the restricted zone. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the physical characteristics of the animal to determine its legal status regarding the Haram's prohibitions.
